We have done this before. 

The first idea was `zen dot velixir dot run`
The second idea was `chaos dot velixir dot run` 

Here was the original instruction for chaos: 

I have a new project in simple asp dotnet blazor server. 
It runs on the free tier of a service called v elixir. 
I have the dump.txt attached with this prompt. 
Some ground rules: 
no css or javascript frameworks 
we write our own css and js 
preferably scoped within the same component 
be very mindful of performance as this needs to run on the free tier. 
can you please write everything that is absolutely essential for the site to function? 

an ephermal message board same as zen but with a twist -- every single message gets stored in the browser local storage as soon as the user gets this information AND when a new user connects, they send everything they have in their local storage back to the server. so every single message has a unique uuid v7 guid. the server takes a look at this list and checks against its own list. if the server has fifty items that are newer than what the client has sent, it does nothing with the list. and the client will dutifully add the items from the server to its local data so locally, the user will continue to see older data even though it is no longer present on the server. the server still only keeps the last fifty messages. you will have to come up with. it is probably better to use indexed db instead of local storage but I will let you decide the exact details. remember, no third party javascript libraries. if we need any javascript, we must write it ourselves. if the server has restarted and the client has something the server does not, the server accepts it as long as it fits in the fifty cap or if the items are newer than what the server has. we should also have a cap for local history so it doesn't bloat phones. implement a limit of 10k messages beyond which we start deleting the oldest messages as we add new ones. I don't expect us to hit this limit in practice but we are writing a good demo app and we want to make sure we teach people the right way to do things. the handshake order is the client sends the fifty most recent from its indexed db. the server breaks ties by keeping what it already has although I expect exact ties to be rare because we have uuidv7 which should be ordered. ALWAYS ALWAYS REJECT MESSAGES FROM THE FUTURE. The server clock is always correct. reconciliation from the client is up to the cap, newest first. Schema versioning for IndexedDB, so a later change doesn’t break existing users.
a shared real time canvas, no need for anything fancy but users should be able to draw using their mouse on a computer or their finger or a stylus on their phone or tablet and everyone sees everything as soon as anyone draws anything. there is one reset button and anyone can press this at any time to clear the canvas. there is no save functionality, there is only one color -- black, and there is only one brush -- solid, and there is only one weight -- you get the idea. it is as simple as possible. Touch scrolling conflict (touch-action: none), palm rejection, and pointer capture. Coordinate system: normalized 0–1 coordinates so phones and desktops agree, plus a fixed aspect ratio and how to handle resizing and device pixel ratio. Late joiner state: a bounded in-memory stroke list, and a decision on whether it’s lost on restart. (decision: yes). Reset behavior with in-flight strokes (an epoch counter solves it).
a page that explains what this website is all about and links to the github repository for this page. the repository will be public so you can assume that the website can link to the github repository. explain why this website exists and all the things it can do. also explain the what we do and how we do it. this page should also have an easy way for the user to clear the indexed db used in our message board without the user having to clear all the local data for the web application. when the user visits the message board again, the indexed db should be created and populated again fresh from the server
remember no third party css js or any third party dependencies
the project will be served at https://chaos.velixir.run/ 
the code will live in public at https://github.com/kusl/chaos-velixir-run
the license will be AGPL-v3  or later 
we will have a FULL unit test suite with xunit v4
and this is a good time as any to clarify dependencies 
we want to minimize the number of third party dependencies 
but we also want the absolute latest version of all nuget dependencies and all github actions versions possible 
so xunit v4  and add a global.json 
which opts into the microsoft testing platform 
{
    "test": {
        "runner": "Microsoft.Testing.Platform"
    }
}

also slnx for solution 
also central package management 
also use latest stable version of csharp version for dotnet 10 

we have previously done something similar with zen-velixir-run 
https://github.com/kusl/zen-velixir-run 
which runs at zen.velixir.run 

this project is much more ambitious
in addition to the blazor server application 
it will also have a full unit test as well as playwright testing suite 

the playwright test suite will need to live in a podman environment 
because my fedora linux is not directly supported by playwright 

also it is critical that we carefully study the existing zen-velixir-run to make sure the application 
deploys perfectly each time. 
I have added a new repository secret to 
https://github.com/kusl/chaos-velixir-run/settings/secrets/actions
called 
VELIXIR_API_KEY
so that part is already in place 

however, except for this one deployment action 
all github actions must be as dumb as possible 
with as much of the logic in shell scripts 
so the core of these actions can be run locally 

and never forget that our application does not have a guaranteed state to save somewhere, because we are still using a free tier, the application may restart at any time 
so we must be resilient to this just like the original zen-velixir-run 

another thing that sets us apart from zen is unlike zen which only has one page, we will have several components and several pages 

we will be able to navigate between the pages 
and we will make use of reusable components 

we will use as little javascript as possible, in fact we will try to avoid it entirely where possible 
we will also use the latest evergreen javascript features where possible 

we will use the latest css features and we will never ever have vendor specific css code and we will never ever use shebang important in our css. if our website is ugly without important we will live with ugly website but we will NEVER EVER use important. also we will compartmentalize our css to our component specific css file where possible but we will also have a global variable file using css. remember, no pre processor no post processor no sass no scss none of that, only evergreen css as available in the current versions of modern browsers 

in fact, absolutely NO legacy code, no legacy polyfill, no support for legacy browsers at all 
however, we will use browser local storage, cookies, and all modern luxuries as afforded 

remember, we will never require users to log in or authenticate in any way because we don't have a stateful backend that persists forever. 

last but not the least, we will have an export.sh that exports all the code into a single dump.txt file just like we do now. this export.sh will live in a scripts folder unlike zen because this project unlike zen will have multiple shell scripts 
all these scripts will have a single parent script when run which will build, run all the tests not just unit tests but also integration tests, run the export shell script that bundles everything together, etc

we will NEVER EVER use any javascript or css library EVER in this application 
users will be able to toggle light and dark mode and the application will keep track of user's choice in local storage. if no setting is found in local storage, the application will respect the user's choice in the browser settings or operating system settings. use blazor's .razor.css isolation for css where possible 
avoid any cookies if at all possible, no cookies means no consent banner which is our goal. 

the interactivity model is blazor server or blazor interactive. static SSR with interactive islands is perfect. about, theme toggle, and navigation should work with zero circuit. only /board and /canvas open a circuit. first party signalR is acceptable but remember everything should be built in don't assume we have any azure infrastructure. blazor.web.js is totally acceptable. and yes, handwritten js is acceptable, when I say no js I mean no third party js but I understand some js is unavoidable. where possible, small dependency free ES modules colocated with their components .razor.js is ideal. 

consistent with the /docs folder where we will have /llm folder, we will also have a /adr folder inside docs which will house architectural decision records. anywhere I have been ambiguous, use your best judgment and record the adr. in our subsequent conversations, you will always keep these ADR up to date. be concise and to the point in the documentation. never write flowery language. 
NEVER EVER EVER write code comments. 
in fact, never, ever write comments at all. 
markdown files such as readme.md are the exception but even these should be as concise and terse as possible.

Rate limits and max connections per IP, message length, stroke point limits, and spam. Without any moderation, the About page should say plainly that content spreads to every client and can’t be recalled.

Security headers and a strict CSP. With no third-party code, you can use default-src 'self' with no inline scripts, which is a nice property to demonstrate. Blazor’s own inline bits might need a nonce, so verify.

Origin checking on the socket endpoint.

Naming and layout: src/Chaos.Web, tests/Chaos.Web.Tests, tests/Chaos.E2E, scripts/.
Directory.Build.props (nullable, warnings as errors, analyzers, deterministic builds), Directory.Packages.props, .editorconfig, and global.json pinning the SDK with rollForward.
The AGPL notice: a LICENSE file, SPDX headers, and the AGPL network-use requirement means the site should visibly link to its source (the About page does this).
Testing JS: how do we unit test the hand-written JS modules without a framework? Options are Playwright tests only, or Node’s built-in test runner, though that adds a Node dependency. Worth deciding. The js will be testable with both playwright as well as the latest version of vitest. Coverage tooling and whether the parent script enforces a threshold. there is no threshold but we do report coverage. 
Playwright in Podman: pin the image version to the NuGet package version, run the app on the host or in a pod, and decide how the test container reaches the app (host networking vs. a pod). --> there should be exactly ONE place where playwright version is declared so if we need to upgrade to a newer version later, it only touches one file. 
Script contract: exit codes, set -euo pipefail, idempotency, a --skip-e2e flag, and the parent script named something like scripts/run-all.sh.
export.sh rules: what to exclude (bin, obj, binary files, the dump itself) and whether it should redact anything. it should exclude all of /docs/llm however it SHOULD include everything else in /docs including ADR. you can't edit what you can't read. no third party code should be included, no microsoft code should be included. 
Dependabot or an equivalent for keeping “absolute latest” versions current. Without it, “latest” is only true on day one. it is ok for it to create pull requests but I might ignore them. 
readme should clarify version this or later to avoid becoming stale. 
Health endpoint, graceful shutdown, ServerGC off and ConcurrentGarbageCollection off for memory, response compression, and ReadyToRun or trimming decisions (check what v elixir actually supports). also check what zen actually does in the included dump 
Logging kept minimal to avoid disk and CPU.
Cold starts on a free tier: the client should show a “waking up the server” state and reconnect with backoff and jitter.
we also need 
A custom 404 page and a “disconnected” banner.
Accessibility: keyboard use of the message board, aria-live for new messages, reduced motion, and a note that the canvas is inherently pointer-based.
Theme toggle behavior before hydration to avoid a flash (this requires a tiny inline script or a CSP-compatible alternative), and color-scheme/light-dark() usage.
Display details: timestamps (UUIDv7 gives you one for free), whether messages have a nickname (probably not), and how “older, no longer on the server” messages are shown differently from live ones. That visual distinction is the heart of the twist. messages do NOT have a nickname. old local messages will have a dotted border instead of solid border that the messages on the server do. 

Delivery
Whole project as one tar.gz, unambiguous file placement
Any files to delete on updates called out explicitly
No bespoke sed/patch scripts — full files only for anything that changes
Docs updated alongside code changes
Low verbosity, no code comments

we don't live there 
our home is at 
https://github.com/kusl/nest
(and yes the github secret is already in place)
which will deploy to 
https://nest.velixir.run/

This website is different. 

It is a way to share links to popular home buying platforms and a way to leave and read comments about these listings 
similar to the other velixir projects, 
there is NO backend here 
while the server will make an effort to store some data, 
the vast majority of the work of storing data will fall on the clients 
and the data will simply disappear if they are older 
or if the server restarts 
so it is critical to write resilient code 
and data structures 
and also algorithms that can somehow intermingle them for lack of a better word 
there will be no authentication or authorization required just like chaos 
and a server restart wipes all the data on the server as usual 
however, when clients connect, then all the data the clients send will be available for all other clients 
as usual, a user can choose to delete all the data on their own browser 
however, that does not delete it on anyone else's browsers
because we only store plain text (utf-8 and critically, all the emojis included in plain text)
we should be able to store a lot of user input 
we also need some basics that a user can enter 
ux is critical 
a typical user is likely on their phone, and juggling between multiple tabs 
but they could be on a desktop computer as well 
so both input formats should be supported 
we need to understand things like zillow id 
and we need to understand links are the same even though they have different query parameters 
for example, 
https://www.zillow.com/homedetails/2893-State-Route-26-Gln-Glen-Aubrey-NY-13777/29747113_zpid/
The Zillow ID (zpid) from that URL is 29747113. 
so this URL includes the address of the home 
but sometimes a link might not have the address 
for example, this is the same listing 
https://www.zillow.com/homedetails/29747113_zpid/
also redfin and realtor dot com have their own schemes 
so we should allow users to add / edit some structured data 
for example, how many bedrooms, how many bathrooms, how many square feet, address, zip code, 
construction date, etc you get the idea 
because we don't have any API access to anything 
we will have to rely on user input for all this data 
the key is to make it as pain free as possible 
and let users to get to writing comments about the listing as possible 
and here is another critical part 
if there are multiple entries for the same address or listing 
for example, maybe someone entered some data went offline 
the data went away 
then someone else came one line and entered some data 
about the same listing 
we should use some magic secret sauce 
well it isn't secret because the whole thing is open source AGPLv3 
but somehow merge them together on a single page 

I have attached the dump of `chaos.velixir.run` 
so you have a running start 

we should write resilient code 
usability, readability, legibility, and responsive design 
we do not have images for any kind of rich formatting 
so it should be straight forward 

as we do all of this 
please be mindful to use best engineering practices 
and solid principles 

Use your best judgment
If only a few files (under five or there about) need to change, give me the full path of the files that need to change and the FULL file 
if there are a lot of files that need to change 
Delivery
    Whole project as one tar.gz, unambiguous file placement
    do not include any file that has not changed 
    Any files to delete on updates called out explicitly

# nest status (2026-11-05)

Repo: https://github.com/kusl/nest, site: https://nest.velixir.run/. Built from the chaos-velixir-run dump.

Delivered: full project as nest.tar.gz (src/Nest.Web, tests/Nest.Web.Tests, tests/Nest.E2E, tests/js, tests/fixtures, scripts, docs/adr 0001-0020).

Design in one line: immutable entries (link, fact, comment) with server UUIDv7 ids, each carrying listing keys (zillow, redfin, realtor, address, url hash); union-find over keys merges homes; newest fact value wins; ids-first handshake (Join snapshot of ids, Fetch missing, Offer what server lacks).

Open items:
- C# was not compiled in the session (no .NET SDK access). JS suite (127 Vitest tests) passed.
- Deploy needs repository variable VELIXIR_APP_ID in addition to the VELIXIR_API_KEY secret.
- LICENSE is the SPDX AGPL-3.0-or-later text; GitHub's copy can replace it.

I’ve built the whole nest project and sent it as nest.tar.gz. One important caveat: the C# has never been compiled. This sandbox can’t download the .NET SDK, so please run scripts/run-all.sh first and send me any build errors. The JavaScript side is tested: all 127 Vitest tests pass.

Unpack it from the repo root: tar -xzf nest.tar.gz -C ~/src/dotnet/nest. It’s a new repo, so there’s nothing to delete. It does include a README.md and LICENSE, which replace any that GitHub created.

How it works

Everything is an entry that never changes. There are three kinds: a link, a set of details, or a comment. The server gives each one a UUIDv7 ID from its own clock. It keeps the newest 1,000; each browser keeps up to 20,000 in IndexedDB.
How homes merge: every entry carries the IDs of its home:
The Zillow ID from the link (29747113_zpid).
The Redfin or Realtor.com ID from the link.
A standardized address: “Street” and “St”, “Route” and “Rte”, “Apt 4” and “#4” all match.
For other sites, a hash of the link with the query string removed.
Any two entries that share one of these IDs end up on the same page. So your example works: a Zillow link with its address merges with a Redfin link added later with the same address. When two people set the same detail, the newest value wins and the previous one is shown next to it. A wrong merge can’t be undone, and the About page says so.
Reconnecting after a restart: the server first sends only the IDs it has. The browser downloads what it’s missing and offers back what the server lacks. The server accepts those only if they’re older than its start time, not from the future, and fit among its newest 1,000.
UX:
Text shared from a phone app works, because the link is found inside it.
Pasting a link to a home you already have opens it instead of adding a duplicate.
The address is pre-filled from Redfin and Realtor.com links. Zillow links mix street and city together, so that one is flagged for you to check.
Bad values are explained next to the field before anything is sent.
Unsent comments survive a reload.
Dotted border means only browsers still have it.
Pages: only the home list (/) and each home’s page open a live connection; About and the 404 page don’t. The About page can delete this browser’s copy without touching the server or anyone else’s.
C# and JavaScript agree: tests/fixtures holds shared JSON test cases for links, addresses, details and merging, and both test suites run them.
What you need to do

Add a repository variable VELIXIR_APP_ID (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables). The deploy needs the velixir app ID, which I don’t have; it fails with a clear message until it’s set.
Vitest is now 5.1.0, the latest; chaos used 5.0.5. The NuGet versions are copied from chaos because I couldn’t check NuGet from here.
LICENSE is the AGPL-3.0-or-later text from the SPDX list, reflowed. Swap in GitHub’s copy if you prefer the official layout.
Decisions where the brief left room are recorded in docs/adr (0001–0020).
